headline: Sellers Dominate Friday Session as Broad Retreat Leaves Few Safe Harbors
body_html:
Midday Friday finds the market under broad pressure, with decliners outpacing advancers by more than three to one across the 545-name universe — 416 stocks lower against just 129 in positive territory. Every sector tracked is in the red, with Software holding up best at a modest decline of 0.37%, while Homebuilders bear the brunt of selling, off 2.34% at the halfway point. Semiconductors and Consumer names are also meaningfully lower, down 1.17% and 1.46% respectively.

The standout story of the session sits within that battered semiconductor group: Skyworks Solutions has surged nearly 9.8% to lead all gainers, joined by Qorvo up 6.77% and Cirrus Logic ahead 5.2%, suggesting company-specific catalysts — likely supply-chain or design-win news — are overriding the sector's broader weakness. Academy Sports + Outdoors rounds out the bright spots, climbing 5.99% against an otherwise difficult consumer tape.

On the downside, American Eagle Outfitters is the session's most dramatic casualty, plunging nearly 14% and dragging fellow apparel name Abercrombie & Fitch down 6%. Into the close, watch whether the RF-chip cluster holds its gains and whether consumer names find footing as traders position ahead of next week's inflation data.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Hold Steady Ahead of Inflation Report
briefs.body: Bond markets are in a holding pattern Friday as traders await upcoming consumer inflation figures. Oil-price pressure is adding a layer of complexity to the inflation calculus, keeping yields anchored rather than pushing them in either direction. The print is expected to be a key catalyst for rate-path sentiment early next week.

briefs.headline: Houthi Advance to Bab el-Mandeb Strait Rattles Shipping Outlook
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthi forces have reached Dhubab, placing them on the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the mouth of a critical global shipping corridor, according to reports. The development raises fresh concerns about maritime traffic disruption and is contributing to elevated geopolitical risk premiums in energy markets today.

briefs.headline: Trump Declines to Back Saudi Push for U.S. Strikes on Houthis
briefs.body: President Trump has reportedly turned down Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's request for direct American military strikes against Houthi positions, according to a report cited by Reuters. The decision signals Washington's reluctance to escalate involvement in the Red Sea conflict even as Gulf tensions intensify.

briefs.headline: UAE Rethinks AI Data-Center Strategy Following Iranian Strikes
briefs.body: The United Arab Emirates has revised its artificial-intelligence data-center expansion plans in the wake of Iranian attacks, according to Reuters sources. The recalibration reflects how the broader regional conflict is reshaping major infrastructure investment decisions across the Gulf, with implications for global AI buildout timelines.

briefs.headline: China Curbs Fuel Price Rises for Third Time Since Iran War Began
briefs.body: Beijing has intervened to limit domestic fuel price increases for the third consecutive time since the outbreak of the Iran conflict, according to Reuters. The move underscores China's effort to insulate its economy from energy-cost pass-throughs while managing inflationary pressures driven by sustained disruption to Gulf oil flows.

briefs.headline: UK Economy Posts Strongest Growth Since Early 2025
briefs.body: Britain's economy expanded at its fastest pace since the opening months of 2025, with Reuters attributing part of the acceleration to a possible artificial-intelligence productivity boost. The reading offers a brighter counterpoint to the geopolitical turbulence weighing on markets elsewhere and could influence Bank of England rate deliberations.
